meta.title: Insider data exfiltration: Northwind Analytics workstation WKS-FIN-07 (SYNTHETIC)
meta.description: Fictional scenario. An employee who has given notice stages customer pricing, a roadmap and a client list, archives them with 7-Zip, renames the archive to look like a holiday photo, copies it to a USB drive, deletes the original archive and two notes, runs a secure-delete tool, and sets back the dates on a staged document.
meta.notice: SYNTHETIC DATA. Every file, timestamp, browser entry, registry value and raw image in this case was generated by a script (forensictriage/synthetic.py). The people, company, devices and domains are fictional; web addresses use reserved or fictional names and IP addresses come from RFC 5737 documentation ranges.

custody.detail: Hashed 38 evidence and reference files before analysis (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256)
Analysed 32 files; parsed 1 browser DB(s), 7 prefetch entries, 14 registry values, 2 Recycle Bin records
Carved 5 candidate file(s) from 1 raw image(s); written under the output folder only
Extracted 12 distinct indicators (282 noise URLs suppressed)
Before and after manifests are identical (SHA-256, MD5, SHA-1, size, mtime, mode): evidence unchanged

integrity.method: All evidence is opened read-only (O_RDONLY, SQLite mode=ro&immutable=1). Every file is hashed (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256) and stat-ed before analysis and again after; any change in content, size, mtime or mode is reported. Outputs are written outside the evidence folders. Access times are not compared because reading can legitimately change them on some file systems.

findings.title: File matches a known-bad hash: invoice_template.pdf
findings.summary: Users/jwhitfield/Downloads/invoice_template.pdf has a hash on the known-bad list (ExfilHelper-stub (synthetic known-bad sample)). SHA-256 eebbcb372c71d91cbcce816b6ab237d5706471bcc6d3a525bb2f12ca0dc5b636.
response: Isolate the host from the network.
Preserve the file and its hashes; submit to your malware analysis process.
Search other hosts for the same hash.

findings.title: Extension does not match content: invoice_template.pdf

response: Treat the file by what it is, not by its name.
Check when and by whom it was renamed (timeline, MFT, USN journal if available).
If it is an archive, list its members and review them.
